item.title: Ryan Cohen Vows GameStop Will Pursue eBay Despite Offer Being Rebuffed
item.description: GameStop Corp. Chief Executive Officer Ryan Cohen declined to say if he planned to raise his $56 billion offer for online auctioneer eBay Inc., but said “we’re coming for eBay one way or another.”

item.title: Oil Traders Crowd Around Cheap TACO Hedge as Iran War Escalates
item.description: An unusual options trade is becoming a favored hedge against the risks of sudden U-turns in US President Donald Trump’s stance on Iran, a dynamic that has repeatedly whipsawed markets in recent months.

item.title: Verizon Cuts Store Workers in Reorganization Strategy
item.description: Verizon Communications Inc. announced a round of layoffs Thursday that will impact about 3,000 employees in corporate-owned retail stores, the latest move in new Chief Executive Officer Dan Schulman’s plan to transform the mobile provider.

item.title: Podcast: Tokenization, Digital Twins and the Future of ETFs
item.description: On this episode of Trillions, we explore how this government transformation will affect stocks, bonds and exchange-traded funds.

item.title: Turning Oil to Fuel Has Never Been More Profitable as Refining Margins Surge
item.description: Profit margins for US refiners making gasoline and diesel from crude oil are shattering records, as fuel supply disruptions driven by war lift prices for refined products.

item.title: Citi Traders Pitch Shorting French Shipping Giant CMA CGM Bonds
item.description: Citigroup’s credit traders and analysts are recommending their hedge fund clients short bonds issued by French shipping giant CMA CGM Group, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Oracle Risks Falling Behind in AI Race as Spending Binge Bites
item.description: Oracle Corp.’s ambitions to dominate the artificial intelligence buildout are running into a key hurdle: funding a spending spree without further damaging its credit standing.

item.title: Paschi Casts Doubts On Intesa Bid, Urges Studying BPM Plan
item.description: Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena SpA expressed broad concerns over a takeover bid by Intesa Sanpaolo SpA while highlighting perceived benefits in a rough rival pitch presented by Banco BPM SpA.

item.title: Carney Taps General Dynamics for $1.4 Billion Canada Armored Vehicle Deal
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney announced the Canadian government is earmarking C$2 billion ($1.4 billion) over four years to build armored combat support vehicles in southwestern Ontario.

item.title: Chevron to Sign Oil Investment Accords With Iraq on Friday
item.description: Chevron Corp. expects to sign accords with Iraq on Friday that will advance its negotiations about investing in large oil fields, according to a senior company executive.

item.title: Nigeria Expects Remittances to Hit $1 Billion a Month by Year-End
item.description: Nigeria anticipates remittances from citizens living abroad to increase by two-thirds over 2026 as it seeks to bolster its foreign-exchange reserves, its central bank governor said.

item.title: Visa Is Expanding Its Crypto Push With New Stablecoin Platform
item.description: Visa Inc. unveiled a platform that lets financial firms issue, move and manage stablecoins, broadening the payments giant’s crypto offerings as banks and fintechs prepare for wider adoption of the digital tokens.

item.title: Balbec Secures $930 Million in Commitments for Asset-Based Credit Fund
item.description: Alternative asset manager Balbec Capital LP has obtained commitments of more than $930 million for its latest flagship fund that will invest in a variety of asset-based credit, according to a filing on Thursday.

item.title: India’s Maruti to Fight Order to Replace Car Over Ethanol Damage
item.description: Maruti Suzuki India Ltd. said it will challenge a consumer court order asking the nation’s largest carmaker to replace a vehicle over alleged damage from ethanol-blended fuel, a case that assumes significance as the debate over the nation’s biofuel push intensifies.

item.title: IMF Cautions Burnham Against Raising UK’s Top Income Tax Rate
item.description: The International Monetary Fund has warned incoming UK prime minister Andy Burnham that raising the top rate of income tax would hurt the economy by discouraging work, and recommended higher rates on the lower paid instead.

item.title: China-Led AI Body Enlists Global South States to Rival US
item.description: Twenty-nine countries including Russia have signed up to join the China-led World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, as Beijing’s plan to jostle with the US for influence over the emergence of artificial intelligence begins to take shape.

item.title: Aston Martin Creditors Tap Jefferies as Debt Worries Grow
item.description: A group of creditors to Aston Martin Lagonda Global Holdings Plc have picked Jefferies Financial Group Inc. as financial adviser as concern over the debt of the distressed British automaker grows, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Fed’s Watchdog Warns On Insider Risk after China Secrets Case
item.description: The Federal Reserve’s internal watchdog warned Thursday the central bank needs to do more to protect sensitive economic information that is being pursued by foreign adversaries.

item.title: Bank of America Exits Chicago Plan to Sell Overdue Parking Debt
item.description: Bank of America is no longer working with Chicago on the sale of debt owed to the city from fines and fees, and officials have been unable to advance the deal so far this year, according to the mayor’s office.

item.title: Ladbrokes Owner Entain to Cut 2% of Staff as UK Taxes Hit
item.description: Entain Plc will cut 500 jobs, or about 2% of its global workforce, as the gambling industry grapples with higher UK taxes, tighter regulation and growing competition from prediction markets.

item.title: Bond Traders Bail on Fed Hike Wagers on Softer Inflation Outlook
item.description: The bullish tone in the US bond market following two benign inflation reports has traders of interest-rate options scrambling to exit positions bought in anticipation of at least one increase by the Federal Reserve this year.

item.title: What Nigeria Stocks Tell Investors About Africa Markets: Live Q&A
item.description: Bloomberg reporters answer your questions about Nigeria’s world-beating stocks, and where investors are finding opportunities in African markets, in a Live Q&A on Friday, July 17 at 12 p.m. GMT

item.title: Faena Condo Project Sells $30 Million Penthouse on Miami River
item.description: Argentine fashion entrepreneur-turned-developer Alan Faena sold a $30 million penthouse in his planned twin condo towers on the Miami River, a milestone in the mission to take his maximalist, theatrical brand worldwide.

item.title: Chile Senate Hands Kast a Win on Key Economic Reform Bill
item.description: Chile’s Senate gave its approval to President José Antonio Kast’s wide-ranging economic bill, clearing a key hurdle for an administration trying to revive the sluggish economy.

item.title: Citigroup Sees Bondholders Recover 50% of Senegal’s Debt Under Revamp
item.description: Holders of Senegal’s dollar bonds could end up recouping less than 50% of the face value of the securities in the event of a restructuring — below the prices at which the debt currently trades, according to Citigroup Inc.

item.title: Canada’s Forgotten Shale Gas Play Reemerges as Oil Hot Spot
item.description: On the edge of the Canadian Rocky Mountains, companies including Obsidian Energy Ltd. and Yangarra Resources Corp. are breathing new life into a long-dormant gas reservoir — except now they’re drilling for oil.

item.title: German Chemical Industry in Crisis Despite Reprieve, Lobby Says
item.description: Germany’s chemical industry remains in a structural crisis despite a brief breather when the conflict in the Middle East triggered stockpiling and hit rivals in Asia harder, according to the industry’s VCI association.

item.title: US Homebuilder Sentiment Slips Again to Match Year’s Low
item.description: Confidence among US homebuilders dropped for a second month to the lowest level of the year, dragged lower by elevated borrowing costs and higher material and land prices.

item.title: Raiffeisen Clears Key Hurdle in €517 Million Bid for Addiko Bank
item.description: Raiffeisen Bank International AG reached a key milestone in its bid to acquire Addiko Bank AG after shareholders representing more than 55% tendered their shares, reaching the offer’s minimum threshold.

item.title: Gaming Bonds Lose Allure as Threat From Prediction Markets Grows
item.description: Investors increasingly see gaming bonds as a losing bet.
